The strong growth in submissions to *Bayesian Analysis* has continued throughout 2026: by the end of August, we had already received 282 submissions, compared with 327 during the whole of 2025, itself a record year for the journal.

Despite this substantial increase in volume, our streak of sending decisions within four months of submission is still alive: we have now cleared all papers submitted through May 31, 2026. Maintaining timely and consistent turnaround times while preserving the constructive and thorough feedback that is part of the *Bayesian Analysis* tradition is becoming increasingly demanding. A big thank you, once again, to our Co-Editors, Associate Editors, and Referees for their dedication and extraordinary efforts for making this possible.

## Lindley Prize

The 2024 [Lindley Prize](https://bayesian.org/project/lindley-prize/) was awarded during the banquet at the [2026 ISBA World Meeting in Nagoya](https://isba2026.github.io/). Congratulations to Jim Griffin, whose paper ["Expressing and Visualizing Model Uncertainty in Bayesian Variable Selection Using Cartesian Credible Sets"](https://doi.org/10.1214/25-BA1568) won the prize, and to Changwoo Lee, Alessandro Zito, Huiyan Sang, and David Dunson, whose paper ["Logistic-Beta Processes for Dependent Random Probabilities with Beta Marginals"](https://doi.org/10.1214/25-BA1541) received an honorable mention. I am also very grateful to all members of the Lindley Prize Committee for their careful and thoughtful work.

With one edition of the prize concluded, it is already time to look ahead to the next one. Papers presented at the [2026 ISBA World Meeting in Nagoya](https://isba2026.github.io/) can be considered for the 2026 Lindley Prize, provided they are submitted to *Bayesian Analysis* by September 30, 2026. Authors should indicate in their cover letter that the paper is being submitted for consideration for the Lindley Prize and provide the identification number of the session in which the work was presented. Let me also add that those who have already submitted an eligible paper without indicating the prize can still enter by contacting me by the same deadline and providing the relevant session information.

## Special Discussion Paper

It is a great pleasure to announce a special discussion paper in *Bayesian Analysis*: ["Dependent Dirichlet Processes"](https://doi.org/10.1214/26-BA1610) by Steven N. MacEachern, his original 2000 manuscript. The paper is accompanied by ["A Modern Perspective on Dependent Dirichlet Processes"](https://doi.org/10.1214/26-BA1610INV0) by Steven N. MacEachern, Juhee Lee, and Hang J. Kim. Together, the two contributions combine the original formulation of what has become a highly influential class of Bayesian nonparametric models with a contemporary perspective on its development and impact.

We now welcome contributed discussions. Contributions may address the original DDP paper, the accompanying contemporary perspective, or more broadly the development, evolution, and future directions of dependent Dirichlet processes and related models. Discussions should be no more than two pages long and prepared using the BA style files, available through the [Bayesian Analysis author resources](https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bayesian-analysis/author-guidelines) on Project Euclid. Please submit your discussion via [EJMS](https://www.e-publications.org/ims/submission/) by October 15, 2026, selecting "Contributed Discussion" as the manuscript type and indicating that the discussion refers to MacEachern's "Dependent Dirichlet Processes" (BA1610).

## September Issue and Advance Publication

The [September issue of *Bayesian Analysis*](https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bayesian-analysis/volume-21/issue-3) has just appeared, featuring 19 papers. Its somewhat larger size reflects our continuing effort to shorten the time between Advance Publication and appearance in a regular issue. I encourage you to explore these contributions, as well as the many excellent papers recently accepted and now available in the [Advance Publication section](https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bayesian-analysis/advance-publication).
